outcome: Maternal morbidity (postpartum hemorrhage, cesarean section rates, length of hospital stay)

Neonatal morbidity (low 5 min APGAR score, need for NICU admission, neonatal convulsions, hyperbilirubinemia, necrotizing enterocolitis, periventricular leukomalacia, septicemia, need for mechanical ventilation, intraventricular hemorrhage, neonatal hypotension, hypothermia, length of NICU stay)
cohort: 100 pregnant women giving preterm birth between 26 and 34 weeks gestation
finding: Antenatal magnesium sulfate administration was associated with a trend toward reduced risk of several neonatal morbidities, including need for mechanical ventilation, intraventricular hemorrhage, and length of NICU stay, without significant increases in maternal morbidity or mortality.
